newsitem.title: USA: Blue-chip issues little changed, techs shine.
newsitem.headline: Blue-chip issues little changed, techs shine.

text.p: High-technology stocks rallied to take centre stage again on Tuesday while blue-chip issues languished.
The Dow Jones industrial average, down as much as 36 points earlier in the session, stood unchanged at 8,198.45, just after 1 p.m. EDT (1700 GMT).
With the Dow looking tired, investors shifted their focus to the technology sector, sending the Nasdaq composite index, laden with high-tech issues, up 13.01 points to 1,618.46.

"Money is going into technology," said Roy Blumberg, chief investment strategist at Josephthal Lyon & Ross. "Dow stocks have been languishing because techs stocks are warming the cockles of everybody's heart."

Tech stocks, which lent support to the broader stock market on Monday in the face of bond market declines, again assumed market leadership. Shares of semiconductor and semiconductor equipment makers moved higher.
"The performance of the technology is mind-boggling," Dick Stein, vice president of U.S. Clearing Corp, said. "They continue to plough ahead."

In the broader market, advancing issues beat decliners by a 7-6 margin on moderate New York Stock Exchange volume of 282 million shares. The Standard & Poor's index of 500 stocks added 2.21 points to 952.51.
The Dow's advance was hampered by investors rotating funds out of blue chips and by weakness in the bond market, analysts said.
"The stock market is still waiting for the bond market to find its footing," Jim Benning, a BT Brokerage trader said.
The 30-year Treasury fell for the third straight session, declining about a quarter point and raising its yield, which moves in the opposite direction, to 6.50 percent from 6.48 percent Monday.

Long-term interest rates have jumped since reports on Friday fanned investor worries about unexpected strength in the economy that could fuel inflation. Bond investors also braced for new supply on Tuesday as the U.S. Treasury was set to auction $16 billion of three-year notes.
Analysts said stock investors shared the bond market's concerns about higher rates because share prices were lofty.

"The stock market is very sensitive to the bond market at these levels," said Henry Herrmann, chief investment officer, Waddell & Reed. "It is in a holding pattern, crunching through numbers to see how much the economy is reaccelerating."

Among tech stocks, Intel Corp. jumped 2-15/16 to 99-11/16 and Microsoft Corp. added 2-2/16 to 143-11/16. As money poured in the sector, shares of Dow stocks Hewlett-Packard Co. and International Business Machines Corp. also rose, adding 1-1/4 to 70-15/16 and 1 to 107-7/16, respectively.

Elsewhere, Micro Warehouse Inc. jumped 3-1/2 to 20-7/8 on Nasdaq, where it was one of the biggest gainers of the session, after the catalogue retailer of computers said earnings jumped 44 percent in the second quarter, beating expectations on Wall Street.
The American Stock Exchange index rose 2.47 to 649.06.
